source_audio_policy: Synthesised-only Strudel output; no sample banks are used, so no sample-bank licence applies. No third-party audio recordings are bundled with this generator; if any ever were, the policy would be CC0 or public domain only.

pattern_authorship.author: itsmygithubacct
pattern_authorship.origin: Original project compositions. The first three patterns were composed on 2026-07-07 for an earlier MIT-licensed game project; exact-string searches found no matching upstream Strudel or public pattern source.
pattern_authorship.recorder: Project-authored browser and Puppeteer integration that calls the external @strudel/web API; no Strudel implementation source is copied or bundled.

tool.name: Strudel
tool.role: external live-coding tool driven headless; NOT linked or bundled into Python
tool.workspace: configured at runtime with STRUDEL_DIR; not bundled
tool.how_invoked: a vite dev server serves a recorder page; system Chrome (via puppeteer-core) loads it, and the page records the Web Audio graph with MediaRecorder. The audio is the OUTPUT of running the tool -- Python never imports Strudel.
tool.note: Strudel's AGPL-3.0 covers the tool's own source. This generator ships none of that source; it ships pattern text (below) and Python that launches the tool as a separate process.

synthesis_policy: Every cue uses only synthesised sources: s("sine"/"sawtooth"/"triangle"/"square") and noise ("white"/"pink"/"brown"). No s("bd"), s("piano"), or any dough-samples / sample bank call appears in any pattern, so the rendered audio carries no sample-bank licence entanglement. This is enforced by test_no_cue_uses_a_sample_bank.
determinism: A MediaRecorder real-time capture is NOT byte-deterministic: two takes of one pattern differ by scheduler jitter and opus encoding. This generator does not claim seeded byte-determinism. Each rendered WAV's SHA-256 is recorded in the manifest as an AS-RENDERED record, not a golden. What is pinned is the exact Strudel pattern text (hashed below), the tempo, and the configured external toolchain.
loop_seam: Loop cues are recorded for an integer number of pattern cycles (seconds = cycles / cps), so the tempo grid lands on the loop point. Seamlessness comes from that cycle math, not from a crossfade. A captured WAV also carries a few ms of real-time latency at its head; the `verify` command reports both.

patterns.note: The original recorder named 20 s; 20 s is 5.6 cycles at 0.28 cps, which does not wrap cleanly. Recorded here as 6 cycles = 21.43 s, the whole-cycle length nearest the nominal, so the per-cycle content wraps clean.

excluded.name: dough-samples and every s("...") sample bank (s("bd"), s("piano"), drum machines, soundfonts)
excluded.reason: Strudel can play sampled instruments, but every sample bank carries its own licence, and mixing those into the output would re-introduce exactly the sample-licence entanglement this project avoids. Pure-synth patterns have none, so no cue uses a sample call. This is the whole reason the patterns are oscillators-and-noise only.

excluded.name: Claiming a seeded byte-deterministic render
excluded.reason: Tempting, because every sibling generator is byte-deterministic under a seed. It would be a lie here: the capture is a real-time MediaRecorder pass with opus encoding, so the bytes vary between takes. The honest pin is the pattern text and workspace, with the output SHA recorded as a fact about one take.
